notes:
Inbound SMB lead from support automation space. Self-serve signup then quick exploratory POC. Primary product interest: hosted API — want fast time-to-value and simple integration with existing Zendesk/Front stack. Key items below:

- Use case: auto-summarize incoming tickets into short agent-friendly summaries, extract structured fields (issue_type, severity, customer_impact, suggested_action).
- Tool calling: want model to propose actions (assign, escalate, close) that can be turned into API calls by our orchestrator. Example: model returns {action: "escalate", assignee: "tier2", reason:"payment failure - high impact"}.
- Structured output: need robust JSON schema; want examples of Redwood's structured output + validation tips. Concerned about hallucinations for structured fields — asked about best-effort vs strict schema enforcement and fallback behaviors.
- Latency/throughput: typical volume 10-20 requests/sec during business hours; low burstiness. Target p50 <150ms, p95 <400ms for inference paths used by agent UI. Willing to accept slightly higher p99 for background summarization jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget tight — interest in cost controls (batching suggestions, cache results for repeated threads). Will start on small hosted plan and may move to Dedicated if scale + SLA required.
- Security: SOC2 required for exportable contracts; SSO/SAML for internal access; audit logging for admin actions. No strict data residency initially — US cloud ok.
- Models: prefer open/quantized models to control cost but want Redwood-verified performance profiles; asked about fallbacks to cheaper variants.

Quotes from call: "We want a no-friction path to get summaries into our agent UI — if it takes more than a day to wire the schema, we're less likely to adopt."

Stubs/links: Sent Postman example and quickstart repo, shared security FAQ link, created RDW-3124 for SE follow-up. Next: SE workshop to build 1-2 templates (summary + structured extractor) using customer's sample tickets, then run 1-week pilot on hosted credits.
